summary: Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1883–1887), where he later held a post from circa 1892 to 1933.

Rudolf Otto worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Göttingen, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held academic posts at Göttingen, Breslau (1914–1917), and Marburg (1917–1929).

Rudolf Otto Franke worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn under August Fick and Franz Kielhorn, later working at Berlin (1890) and as professor at the University of Königsberg (1895–1927).

Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1853 to 1856 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Steiner worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at TU Wien (~1879–1883) and the University of Rostock (~1891), and held a post at the Goethe and Schiller Archives from circa 1890 to 1896.

Rudolf Stübe worked in religious studies. He completed his studies across the University of Rostock, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin between 1890 and 1894, studying under Richard Pischel.

Rudolf Thomas Siegfried was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and in Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin (1858–1862).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Basel, Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Berlin under Heinrich Zimmer, and Paris under Henri Gaidoz. He held posts at Jena, the University of Freiburg (1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (1913–1923).

Rudolf Westphal was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Marburg and Tübingen under Johann Gildemeister, later holding posts at Tübingen, Breslau (1857–1862), Fellin Landesschule, Goldingen Gymnasium, and Katkov Lyceum (1875–1881).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Tübinger Stift and under Heinrich Ewald and Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudolph Rahmann studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna, learning from Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers. He held posts at Fu Jen Catholic University, University of San Carlos, and as Professor of Ethnology at Fribourg (1956–1960).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala and Curator at ORI Mysore.

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University under Paul Harrison, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and others, and is attested as a faculty member at Peking University in 2026.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and served on the faculty at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his education at Lund University and the University of Ceylon, and later served as a lecturer at Lund University.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held longtime posts at the University of Bristol and served at the Pali Text Society.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. She has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago and under D. T. Suzuki, Mukai Kono, Sokei-an, and Zuigan Goto, later serving as director of the First Zen Institute of America.

Ruth Gamble specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at RMIT and the Australian National University. She held posts at the University of Munich, the Australian National University, and La Trobe University, where she became Deputy Director in 2024.
Ruth Norton Albright was a scholar of Indology. She completed her doctoral studies at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1915 to 1921, studying under Maurice Bloomfield.
